paper: Gustaw K, Michalak M, Polak-Berecka M, Waśko A. Genome and Pangenome Analysis of Lactobacillus hilgardii FLUB — A New Strain Isolated from Mead. Int J Mol Sci 22(7):3780 (2021). DOI: 10.3390/ijms22073780

open_questions.q: How prevalent is the FLUB flavor/aroma-producing (FLUB-associated) gene cluster across the broader Lentilactobacillus hilgardii species, and is its distribution consistent with vertical inheritance or with horizontal gene transfer from a co-fermenting taxon (Oenococcus, Lactobacillus brevis, Saccharomyces-associated mobilome)?
open_questions.basis: This replication reproduced FLUB's ~266 strain-unique gene count (260–268 across two independent pipelines) but did NOT verify the functional identity of those singletons. The paper interprets several as flavor/aroma-related, arsenic detox, and surface-layer proteins, yet cluster prevalence across a larger L. hilgardii cohort and the GC/codon-usage/synteny signatures needed to distinguish vertical inheritance from HGT were never assessed here. With only n=5 genomes, HGT direction is unidentifiable.
next_steps: Pull all ≥50 currently public L. hilgardii genomes (2026 RefSeq/GenBank + MGnify MAGs) and re-run the Prodigal+mmseqs2 pangenome at n≈50 to measure cluster prevalence.
For each singleton/low-frequency cluster observed in FLUB, compute GC deviation vs. host genome, codon adaptation index, and flanking synteny against the L. hilgardii core to flag HGT candidates.
Query mobile-element databases (ISFinder, ICEberg, PHASTER) around the FLUB-unique cluster loci to look for transposases/integrases/prophage signatures.
BLAST FLUB-unique gene sequences against Oenococcus oeni, L. brevis, and wine/mead-associated Saccharomyces genomes to test the cross-taxon HGT hypothesis.

open_questions.q: Does strain-level divergence within L. hilgardii reflect terroir (geographic/substrate origin: wine grape, mead honey, silage, beverage) or process (fermentation temperature, ethanol, sugar regime) as the dominant driver, and can pangenome-wide association testing separate the two?
open_questions.basis: The paper introduces FLUB as a mead spoilage isolate and contrasts it with the wine-derived ATCC 8290 lineage. Our ANI matrix confirmed FLUB is closest to ATCC 27305 (99.77%) and only ~96.9% ANI from the ATCC 8290/DSM 20176/LH500 wine cluster — consistent with substrate-linked divergence, but n=5–6 genomes with sparse and unstructured metadata cannot separate the terroir signal from the process signal. Isolation-source metadata for many public L. hilgardii deposits is incomplete or free-text-only.
next_steps: Curate isolation-source metadata (substrate, geography, temperature/ethanol/sugar regime, year) for every public L. hilgardii genome by cross-referencing BioSample, source papers, and culture collection records.
Run a pangenome-wide association study (Pyseer / treeWAS / Scoary) with substrate and process covariates, controlling for phylogeny using the core-genome ML tree.
Compute F_ST-analog statistics on core-gene SNPs partitioned by substrate vs. by geography to quantify which factor explains more variance.
Test whether FLUB's singleton set is enriched in genes co-varying with the mead niche (honey sugars, high-fructose, low nitrogen) vs. the wine niche.

open_questions.q: How conserved are secondary-metabolite biosynthesis gene clusters (NRPS, PKS, RiPP, terpenoid, bacteriocin) across L. hilgardii and its sister species (L. buchneri, L. parabuchneri, L. diolivorans, L. brevis), and does FLUB carry any BGCs not seen in the wine-derived reference lineage?
open_questions.basis: This replication measured gene-cluster counts (pangenome partition, singletons) but did NOT run any secondary-metabolite biosynthetic-gene-cluster prediction (antiSMASH, DeepBGC, GECCO). The paper mentions functional categories qualitatively but does not report BGC inventories, and cross-species comparison is entirely absent from both the paper and this replication.
next_steps: Run antiSMASH 7 and DeepBGC on FLUB and all L. hilgardii + sister-species genomes to produce a BGC catalog.
Cluster the BGCs with BiG-SCAPE/BiG-SLiCE to define gene-cluster families (GCFs) and measure per-GCF conservation across the L. hilgardii pangenome and across sister species.
For any FLUB-specific GCF, verify with manual synteny inspection and blastp against MIBiG to identify likely product class.
Cross-check bacteriocin predictions against BAGEL4 as an orthogonal caller.

open_questions.q: Which pangenome-derived genetic biomarkers predict industrial fermentation-performance traits (ethanol tolerance, sugar utilization, fructophily, low-temperature growth, biofilm/surface-layer profile) well enough to serve as starter-culture selection markers for L. hilgardii?
open_questions.basis: The paper's Bioscreen C wet-lab assays show FLUB is more ethanol/sugar tolerant than the reference and is fructophilic. Those phenotype data exist only in the paper — we did not reproduce them, and no pangenome-wide GWAS linking L. hilgardii genotype to fermentation phenotype has been published for a sample size large enough to yield robust biomarkers. Our replication documents the genomic substrate for such an analysis but not the analysis itself.
next_steps: Assemble a phenotype panel across ≥30 L. hilgardii isolates: MIC-style ethanol/sugar tolerance, fructose:glucose preference index, growth curves at 15/25/37 °C, biofilm assay.
Run Pyseer/treeWAS on unitigs and gene presence/absence from the expanded pangenome against each phenotype, controlling for phylogeny.
Validate the top biomarkers by targeted knockout/complementation in FLUB (or a tractable surrogate strain) — this is the wet-lab step that closes the loop.

Cross-reference biomarker hits with the paper's qualitative interpretation of FLUB's singleton set (arsenic detox, surface-layer proteins, metabolic cluster) to test whether the paper's a priori candidates survive an unbiased GWAS.

open_questions.q: What is the full oxidative-stress and ethanol-tolerance gene repertoire of L. hilgardii (Fe/Mn-SOD, catalase, thioredoxin/glutaredoxin systems, Nox NADH oxidase, membrane lipid remodeling, GroEL/DnaK chaperones, F1F0-ATPase composition), how variable is it across strains, and what does that imply for industrial scale-up in high-ethanol/high-sugar/high-oxygen fermentations?
open_questions.basis: This is one of the paper's biological motivations (FLUB's ethanol/sugar tolerance), but a systematic per-gene inventory of oxidative-stress and ethanol-response machinery across the L. hilgardii pangenome was not attempted here — we stopped at partition counts. Nor was scale-up-relevant modeling (e.g. flux-balance or dynamic tolerance modeling) attempted.
next_steps: Build a curated HMM library for the oxidative-stress / ethanol-response gene families (KEGG modules M00119, M00538, M00151; plus lipid remodeling operons) and hmmsearch it against every L. hilgardii proteome.
Score each strain on a per-family presence/copy-number vector; test whether FLUB's vector is an outlier vs. the wine-isolate cluster.
Build a genome-scale metabolic model of FLUB (COBRApy / carveme) and run FBA under high-ethanol and high-fructose constraints to predict scale-up bottlenecks (ATP maintenance, redox balance).
Cross-check predictions against public transcriptomes for L. hilgardii or closest-neighbor species under ethanol/sugar stress to prioritize genes for targeted engineering.
